claims.text: Incorporating a high-temperature-stable, self-lubricating secondary phase into CoCrFeNi will enable formation of an adaptive tribofilm during sliding.
The adaptive tribofilm will maintain low friction from room temperature to 800 °C.
The adaptive tribofilm will maintain low wear from room temperature to 800 °C.
The introduced secondary phase can remain stable and reactive across the full temperature range.
Secondary-phase particles will produce an adaptive, lubricious tribofilm at the sliding interface.
At lower temperatures, the dispersed secondary phase will provide baseline friction reduction.
Increasing temperature will activate a transformation of the secondary phase.
The thermally activated transformation will form a continuous lubricious tribofilm.
The tribofilm will reduce friction by providing a shearable interfacial layer.
The tribofilm will reduce wear by protecting the substrate against abrasion.
Secondary-phase-containing CoCrFeNi will have a lower coefficient of friction than monolithic CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Secondary-phase-containing CoCrFeNi will have a lower wear rate than monolithic CoCrFeNi at every tested temperature from room temperature to 800 °C.
Improved tribological performance is expected under moderate-to-high loads when the environment does not cause extreme oxidation or lubricant-phase degradation.
Excessive mechanical stress may destabilize the tribofilm.
Highly aggressive atmospheres may destabilize the tribofilm.
Analogous self-lubricating systems support the proposed mechanism through formation of lubricious oxides at approximately 704 °C.
